We will construct our prediction-independent groups from { ± 1 } \{\pm 1\} -valued orthogonal systems. The key idea is that orthogonal systems let us “test” the forecaster’s behavior in many independent directions simultaneously. If the forecaster has small calibration error on all groups in an orthogonal family, we can use Parseval’s identity to conclude that the forecaster’s aggregate deviation from honest predictions must be small. These orthogonal systems will be used in two different roles: (i) globally on the mean grid (where we will instantiate a specific system, the Walsh system), and (ii) locally within time blocks that we will specify later (where any Hadamard system suffices).
